body_html:
Passed 2025-04-11. Reading generated by ollama:deepseek-v4-pro from the enrolled text; the full text is at the foot of this page so every statement can be checked against it. LegiScan record · official text

What it does

This North Dakota law requires a prominent disclaimer on political communications and advertising that contain digital content created in whole or in part with artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human. It exempts certain uses of artificial intelligence for text generation, grammar, spelling, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation. It defines artificial intelligence for this purpose.

Who it applies to

  • Any person or entity taking an action for a political purpose, including communication and political advertising in support of or opposition to a candidate, political committee, or political party, or promoting passage or defeat of initiated or referred measures or petitions (Sec. 1)

Effective date

not stated in the text

Key definitions

  • artificial intelligence: a machine based system capable of creating images, graphics, videos, audio, text, and other digital content based on human defined objectives or data patterns; the term does not include systems that are explicitly programmed with rules or tools solely designed to assist with grammar, spelling, or word suggestions without generating human likeness or voice (Sec. 3)

Obligations

  • Any action taken for a political purpose containing images, graphics, videos, audio, text, or other digital content created in whole or in part with the use of artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human must prominently state the following disclaimer: "THIS CONTENT GENERATED BY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE." (Sec. 1)

Prohibitions

  • not stated in the text

Penalties and enforcement

The text does not state who enforces this section, what penalties apply, or whether there is a private right of action (Sec. 1 through Sec. 3).

How it affects AI deployment

  • An organization deploying artificial intelligence to create political advertising or communication that visually or audibly impersonates a human must prominently display the disclaimer "THIS CONTENT GENERATED BY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE." (Sec. 1)
  • An organization using artificial intelligence solely for text generation, grammar correction, spelling checks, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation of human likeness or voice is not required to include the disclaimer (Sec. 2)
  • An organization using systems explicitly programmed with rules or tools solely designed to assist with grammar, spelling, or word suggestions without generating human likeness or voice is not using artificial intelligence as defined by this section (Sec. 3)

Notable exemptions

  • Content solely using artificial intelligence for text generation, grammar correction, spelling checks, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation of human likeness or voice (Sec. 2)
  • Systems explicitly programmed with rules or tools solely designed to assist with grammar, spelling, or word suggestions without generating human likeness or voice are not artificial intelligence under this section (Sec. 3)

Compliance steps

  • Determine whether the action is taken for a political purpose, including communication and political advertising in support of or opposition to a candidate, political committee, or political party, or promoting passage or defeat of initiated or referred measures or petitions (Sec. 1)
  • Assess whether the content contains images, graphics, videos, audio, text, or other digital content created in whole or in part with the use of artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human (Sec. 1)
  • If the content does visually or audibly impersonate a human, prominently state the disclaimer "THIS CONTENT GENERATED BY ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE." (Sec. 1)
  • Confirm whether the artificial intelligence use falls within the exception for text generation, grammar correction, spelling checks, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without creating a new impersonation of human likeness or voice, in which case no disclaimer is required (Sec. 2)
  • Verify that any system used is not excluded from the definition of artificial intelligence because it is explicitly programmed with rules or tools solely designed to assist with grammar, spelling, or word suggestions without generating human likeness or voice (Sec. 3)

Sixty-ninth Legislative Assembly of North Dakota
 In Regular Session Commencing Tuesday, January 7, 2025

 HOUSE BILL NO. 1167
 (Representatives Warrey, Bahl, Christianson, Christy, Dobervich, Vollmer)
 (Senators Meyer, Weber, Sickler)


AN ACT to create and enact a new section to chapter 16.1-10 of the North Dakota Century Code,
 relating to artificial intelligence disclosure statements.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATIVE ASSEMBLY OF NORTH DAKOTA:

 SECTION 1. A new section to chapter 16.1-10 of the North Dakota Century Code is created and
enacted as follows:
 Use of artificial intelligence - Disclosure - Exception - Definition.
 1. Any action taken for a political purpose, including communication and political advertising in
 support of or opposition to a candidate, political committee, or a political party, or for the
 purpose of promoting passage or defeat of initiated or referred measures or petitions,
 containing images, graphics, videos, audio, text, or other digital content created in whole or in
 part with the use of artificial intelligence to visually or audibly impersonate a human,
 prominently must state the following disclaimer: "THIS CONTENT GENERATED BY
 ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE."
 2. This section does not apply to content solely using artificial intelligence for text generation,
 grammar correction, spelling checks, stylistic editing, or enhancing existing content without
 creating a new impersonation of human likeness or voice.
 3. For purposes of this section, "artificial intelligence" means a machine-based system capable
 of creating images, graphics, videos, audio, text, and other digital content based on human-
 defined objectives or data patterns. The term does not include systems that are explicitly
 programmed with rules or tools solely designed to assist with grammar, spelling, or word
 suggestions without generating human likeness or voice.
